# Appeal of Denial — Lower Back (Lumbar) Fusion (CPT 22612)

**RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination**
**Governing Policy:** 2025 Evolent Clinical Guidelines for Medical Necessity Review – HMSA Musculoskeletal Surgery Guidelines ([https://www1.radmd.com/sites/default/files/2025-07/2025%20Evolent%20Musculoskeletal%20Surgery%20Guidelines%20-%20HMSA%20FINAL%20eff%20070125.pdf](https://www1.radmd.com/sites/default/files/2025-07/2025%20Evolent%20Musculoskeletal%20Surgery%20Guidelines%20-%20HMSA%20FINAL%20eff%20070125.pdf))
**Member:** Quinn Foster
**Member ID:** W310107367
**Plan:** HMSA (Hawaii Medical Service Association), Commercial/ACA, State of Hawaii
**Date of Denial Notice:** 2026-08-05
**Reference Number:** POC-D89C6A76F0-15779

Dear HMSA Member Advocacy & Appeals,

I am appealing the denial of my request for a lower back (lumbar) fusion, CPT code 22612. I received a notice dated 2026-08-05 stating that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I am asking HMSA to reconsider this decision. My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary based on my imaging and my history of treatment that has not resolved my symptoms.

## Why I believe this denial should be reconsidered

I want to be transparent about something I noticed when I reviewed the criteria referenced in connection with my denial. The excerpts I have been given from the HMSA Musculoskeletal Surgery Guidelines are all drawn from the sections titled "Cervical Fusion for Treatment of Axial Neck Pain," "Cervical Posterior Decompression with Fusion," and "Cervical Posterior Decompression." For example, one of those excerpts states:

> "Imaging studies confirm the presence of spinal cord or spinal nerve root compression (disc herniation or foraminal stenosis) at multiple levels corresponding with the clinical findings."

My procedure, however, is a **lumbar** fusion, not a cervical procedure. I have not been shown the specific lumbar fusion criteria section of the guideline, so I am not able to confirm that the correct criteria were applied to my request, and I do not want to assume criteria that have not been shown to me. I am asking HMSA to identify and apply the lumbar fusion criteria that actually govern CPT 22612, and to explain how my records were measured against those criteria.

That said, the general principle reflected in the excerpt above — that imaging should confirm spinal nerve root compression corresponding to the clinical findings — is directly supported by my own records, even though it comes from the cervical section:

- **Imaging:** My MRI of the lumbar spine, performed 2026-05-28, shows an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root.
- **Corresponding clinical findings:** I have radicular pain radiating into my right calf, cannot stand for more than 10 minutes, and my exam showed positive provocative testing on the affected side along with a neurologic deficit corresponding to the level shown on imaging.

I also want to note that another excerpt provided references failure of conservative treatment, defined in part as:

> "Lack of meaningful improvement after a full course of treatment;"

My records show that I completed 8 weeks of supervised physical therapy (24 visits, 2026-05-14 to 2026-07-09) focused on core stabilization and lumbar flexibility, documented in my physical therapy discharge note. I also used NSAIDs for 8 months without adequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-11 gave only 2 weeks of partial relief. My symptoms have persisted for 12 months and have not meaningfully improved despite this course of conservative care.

Given the imaging findings confirming nerve root compression at the level corresponding to my symptoms, and the documented lack of meaningful improvement after a full course of conservative treatment, I do not believe the stated reason for denial — that imaging does not support medical necessity — reflects the actual record. I am asking that HMSA review my file against the correct, lumbar-specific section of its own guideline, and reconsider the denial in light of the evidence above.

## What I am requesting

1. A full reconsideration of the denial of CPT 22612 for Quinn Foster, Member ID W310107367, reference number POC-D89C6A76F0-15779.
2. Written identification of the specific lumbar fusion criteria HMSA applied in reviewing this request, since the criteria referenced in the materials available to me address cervical, not lumbar, spine surgery.
3. Confirmation of receipt of this appeal and the timeline for a decision.

I understand my appeal must be received by 2027-02-01. I am submitting it in writing as instructed:

By mail: HMSA Member Advocacy & Appeals, Appeals Coordinator, P.O. Box 1958, Honolulu, HI 96805-1958
By fax: 808-952-7546 or 808-948-8206 (Oahu)
By phone: The number listed in my Guide to Benefits

I understand that if this internal appeal is not resolved in my favor, I may have the right to request an external (IRO) review within 130 days, as described in my denial letter, which remains the authoritative source for my appeal rights.

Please let me know if you need any additional records from me or from Dr. Okafor's office. Thank you for reconsidering my case.

Sincerely,

**Quinn Foster**
Member ID: W310107367
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]
[Date]
